sentences.text: Choose an anchor for the bottom you’ll use.

A fluke anchor, often called a Danforth, is light, stows flat, and holds very well in sand and mud, which makes it the most common anchor on Florida fishing boats, but it can struggle in grass and rock.
A plow or claw anchor holds in most bottoms and resets itself if the wind shifts.
A mushroom anchor works by suction in soft mud and is used for permanent moorings.
A grapnel hooks into rocks and wrecks and is popular for fishing structure on small boats, but it can foul, so rig it to break free.
